intro: Hi! Today you learn the small words that say when and where: at, on and in for times and dates, everyday phrases like in the morning and at night, and in, on, under, next to, between and behind for places. Warm-up: is it 'in Monday' or 'on Monday'?
teachingNotes: Time: at + an exact time (at seven o'clock, at noon, at midnight), on + days and dates (on Monday, on 17 August), in + longer periods: months, years, seasons (in May, in 2026, in the rainy season). Learners met at/on/in briefly in A0 Time & Dates; here they extend and drill it. Use 'small to big': at → on → in. Admit the exceptions to 'small to big': in the morning/afternoon/evening (shorter than a day, but 'in') and at night; present them as fixed chunks, and 'at night' alongside 'at noon / at midnight'.

Indonesian uses 'pada', 'di' or nothing at all (hari Senin, bulan Mei), so learners guess. The most common errors: 'in Monday' (→ on Monday), 'at May' (→ in May), 'in this morning' and 'on every Monday' (no preposition before this, every, tomorrow, yesterday, today).

Parts of the day: in the morning / in the afternoon / in the evening, but at night. With a named day use on: on Sunday morning, not 'in Sunday morning'. At the weekend (British) and on the weekend (American) are both correct; 'in the weekend' is wrong. Indonesian 'malam' can be evening (after about 6 p.m., awake) or night (sleeping time).

Place: in (inside), on (on top of, touching a surface, also on the wall), under, next to, between (two things: between A and B) and behind. Indonesian adds 'di' (di bawah, di sebelah), so learners write 'in under the table' or 'at next to the bank': English uses one preposition only. Also: Indonesian 'di' alone can be in, on or at (di kulkas = in the fridge, di meja = on the table, di rumah = at home), and 'on' covers walls and other surfaces, not only 'di atas'. Explain 'preposition' as 'kata depan' (kata kecil seperti di, ke, pada).

Combine place words with there is / there are from the previous lesson (There is a cat under the table) and with be (The keys are in my bag). Grammar limits: present simple, present continuous, there is/are, can and was/were only; no will or going to. Don't teach in front of, opposite, above/over, for/during/since or at for places beyond known chunks (at home, at school, at the office).

keyPoints.title: at, on, in with times and dates
keyPoints.explanation: at + an exact time (at eight o'clock, at noon). on + a day or a date (on Friday, on 17 August). in + a month, a year or a season (in December, in 2026, in the dry season). Think small to big: at → on → in.

examples.en: The film starts at eight o'clock.
We have a test on Friday.
My sister's wedding is in December.

id.title: at, on, in untuk waktu dan tanggal
id.explanation: at + waktu yang pasti (at eight o'clock, at noon). on + hari atau tanggal (on Friday, on 17 August). in + bulan, tahun, atau musim (in December, in 2026, in the dry season). Ingat dari kecil ke besar: at → on → in.

keyPoints.title: Where things are
keyPoints.explanation: Use be + in (inside), on (on top, touching), under, next to, between (two things) or behind. Use only one preposition: under the table, not 'in under the table'.

examples.en: The keys are in my bag.
There is a clock on the wall.
The bus stop is next to the school.

id.title: Letak benda
id.explanation: Pakai be + in (di dalam), on (di atas, menempel), under (di bawah), next to (di sebelah), between (di antara dua benda) atau behind (di belakang). Pakai satu preposisi saja: under the table, bukan 'in under the table'.

keyPoints.title: Everyday time expressions
keyPoints.explanation: in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening, but at night. at the weekend (British) or on the weekend (American). With a day, use on: on Friday evening. No preposition before this, every or tomorrow: this morning, every Sunday.

examples.en: My father reads the news in the evening.
The street is quiet at night.
We visit Grandma at the weekend.
examples.id: Kami mengunjungi Nenek di akhir pekan.

id.title: Ungkapan waktu sehari-hari
id.explanation: in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening, tapi at night. at the weekend (British) atau on the weekend (Amerika). Kalau ada nama hari, pakai on: on Friday evening. Tanpa preposisi sebelum this, every, atau tomorrow: this morning, every Sunday.

assessment.rubric: Correct: on (a date). 'in' = 0 (in is for the whole month: in June). 'at' = 0.

assessment.rubric: Correct: at (an exact clock time). 'in' or 'on' = 0.

assessment.rubric: Correct: between (in the middle of two places). 'next to' = 40 (true, but it needs one place, not two). 'behind' = 0.

assessment.rubric: Correct: at (at night is a fixed phrase). 'in' = 0 (common mistake: 'in night'). 'on' = 0.

assessment.rubric: Correct: on (a named day + part of the day takes on). 'in' = 0 (common mistake: 'in Monday morning'). 'at' = 0.

blocks.text: Indonesian often uses *pada* or no word at all (*hari Senin*, *bulan Mei*). English needs a small word before the time. These small words are called **prepositions** (*kata depan*, like *di, ke, pada*). For time there are three: **at** for an exact time (*at seven o'clock*, *at noon*), **on** for days and dates (*on Monday*, *on 17 August*), and **in** for longer times: months, years and seasons (*in May*, *in 2026*, *in the rainy season*).

id.text: Bahasa Indonesia sering memakai *pada* atau tidak memakai kata apa pun (*hari Senin*, *bulan Mei*). Bahasa Inggris butuh kata kecil sebelum waktunya. Kata-kata kecil ini disebut **preposisi** (*kata depan*, seperti *di, ke, pada*). Untuk waktu ada tiga: **at** untuk waktu yang tepat (*at seven o'clock*, *at noon*), **on** untuk hari dan tanggal (*on Monday*, *on 17 August*), dan **in** untuk waktu yang lebih panjang: bulan, tahun dan musim (*in May*, *in 2026*, *in the rainy season*).

rows.en: The shop opens at nine o'clock.
We have lunch at noon.
rows.id: Kami makan siang jam dua belas siang.

rows.en: I have English class on Wednesday.
rows.id: Saya ada kelas bahasa Inggris hari Rabu.

rows.en: Mother's Day in Indonesia is on 22 December.
rows.id: Hari Ibu di Indonesia tanggal 22 Desember.

rows.en: The rainy season starts in November.

blocks.text: Think small to big: **at** a point on the clock → **on** a day → **in** a month, a year or a season. Common mistakes: 'in Monday' (say **on Monday**) and 'at May' (say **in May**).

id.text: Pikirkan dari kecil ke besar: **at** untuk satu titik di jam → **on** untuk satu hari → **in** untuk bulan, tahun atau musim. Kesalahan yang sering terjadi: 'in Monday' (seharusnya **on Monday**) dan 'at May' (seharusnya **in May**).

blocks.prompt: Complete: Our office party is ___ Friday.
blocks.explain: Friday is a day, and days take on: on Friday.

id.explain: Friday adalah nama hari, dan hari memakai on: on Friday.
id.prompt: Lengkapi: Our office party is ___ Friday.

blocks.text: Parts of the day take **in the**: **in the morning**, **in the afternoon**, **in the evening**. Night is different: **at night**. For Saturday and Sunday together, say **at the weekend** (British) or **on the weekend** (American); both are fine. When you name the day, use **on**: **on Friday evening**, **on Sunday morning**.

id.text: Bagian hari memakai **in the**: **in the morning**, **in the afternoon**, **in the evening**. Malam berbeda: **at night**. Untuk Sabtu dan Minggu, ucapkan **at the weekend** (Inggris Britania) atau **on the weekend** (Inggris Amerika); keduanya benar. Kalau kamu menyebut nama harinya, pakai **on**: **on Friday evening**, **on Sunday morning**.

rows.en: I drink coffee in the morning.
The children play outside in the afternoon.
rows.id: Anak-anak bermain di luar sore hari.

rows.en: We watch TV in the evening.

id.note: setelah kira-kira jam 6 sore, sebelum tidur

rows.en: The street is quiet at night.
The market is busy on Sunday morning.
rows.note: day + part of the day → on

blocks.text: No **in / on / at** before **this, every, tomorrow, yesterday** or **today**: *this morning*, *every Monday*, *tomorrow evening*, not 'in this morning' or 'on every Monday'. And Indonesian *malam* is two English words: **evening** (after about 6 p.m., awake) and **night** (when people sleep).

id.text: Jangan pakai **in / on / at** sebelum **this, every, tomorrow, yesterday** atau **today**: *this morning*, *every Monday*, *tomorrow evening*, bukan 'in this morning' atau 'on every Monday'. Dan *malam* dalam bahasa Inggris ada dua: **evening** (setelah sekitar jam 6 sore, masih beraktivitas) dan **night** (waktu orang tidur).

blocks.text:
**Why 'at night' but 'in the morning'?** There's no perfect reason; these are fixed chunks, and they break the 'small to big' rule (a morning is shorter than a day, but it takes *in*). Two tricks to remember:
- **at** goes with 'points' you name: *at noon*, *at midnight*, *at night*.
- If a **day name** is there, the day decides and you use **on**: *in the morning*, but *on Sunday morning*.

id.text:
**Kenapa 'at night' tapi 'in the morning'?** Tidak ada alasan yang sempurna; ini ungkapan tetap, dan tidak ikut aturan 'kecil ke besar' (pagi lebih pendek dari satu hari, tapi memakai *in*). Dua trik supaya ingat:
- **at** dipakai untuk 'titik' waktu yang punya nama: *at noon*, *at midnight*, *at night*.
- Kalau ada **nama hari**, harinya yang menentukan dan kamu pakai **on**: *in the morning*, tapi *on Sunday morning*.

blocks.prompt: Complete: Pak Joko has a short sleep ___ the afternoon.
blocks.explain: Parts of the day take in the: in the afternoon. Only night is different: at night. (No day name here, so not on.)

id.explain: Bagian hari memakai in the: in the afternoon. Hanya malam (night) yang berbeda: at night. (Tidak ada nama hari di sini, jadi bukan on.)
id.prompt: Lengkapi: Pak Joko has a short sleep ___ the afternoon.

blocks.text: To say where something is, use **be** (is / are) + a place word: **in** (inside), **on** (on a surface, touching it), **under**, **next to**, **between** (two things: *between A and B*) and **behind**. Indonesian adds *di* (*di bawah*, *di sebelah*), but in English the preposition already includes the *di*: *under the table*, not 'in under the table'.

id.text: Untuk mengatakan di mana sesuatu berada, pakai **be** (is / are) + kata tempat: **in** (di dalam), **on** (di permukaan, menempel), **under** (di bawah), **next to** (di sebelah), **between** (di antara dua hal: *between A and B*) dan **behind** (di belakang). Bahasa Indonesia menambahkan *di* (*di bawah*, *di sebelah*), tapi dalam bahasa Inggris preposisinya sudah termasuk *di*: *under the table*, bukan 'in under the table'.

rows.en: The milk is in the fridge.
Your glasses are on the table.
The ball is under the car.
The mosque is next to the school.
Sari sits between Budi and Dewi.
rows.id: Sari duduk di antara Budi dan Dewi.

rows.en: The garden is behind the house.

blocks.text: Use one preposition only: 'The bag is in under the table' → **The bag is under the table.** And **on** means touching a surface: a glass **on** the table stands on it, and a clock **on** the wall hangs on it. So **on** is not always *di atas*.

id.text: Pakai satu preposisi saja: 'The bag is in under the table' → **The bag is under the table.** Dan **on** berarti menempel di permukaan: gelas yang **on** the table berdiri di atasnya, dan jam yang **on** the wall tergantung di dinding. Jadi **on** tidak selalu *di atas*.

blocks.text: Indonesian *di* alone can be **in**, **on** or **at** in English. Don't translate *di* by itself; look at where the thing really is: *di kulkas* (inside) → **in** the fridge, *di meja* (on top) → **on** the table, *di dinding* → **on** the wall.

id.text: Kata *di* saja dalam bahasa Indonesia bisa menjadi **in**, **on** atau **at** dalam bahasa Inggris. Jangan terjemahkan *di* sendirian; lihat posisi bendanya yang sebenarnya: *di kulkas* (di dalam) → **in** the fridge, *di meja* (di atasnya) → **on** the table, *di dinding* → **on** the wall.

blocks.prompt: Kuncinya di dalam tas. → The key is ___ the bag.
blocks.explain: di dalam = inside, so in: The key is in the bag.

id.explain: di dalam = inside, jadi in: The key is in the bag.
id.prompt: Kuncinya di dalam tas. → Lengkapi: The key is ___ the bag.

blocks.text: Put it together with **there is / there are**: say what is in the room, then where it is. *There is a sofa in the living room. There is a TV on the wall. My cat is under the sofa.*

id.text: Gabungkan dengan **there is / there are**: sebutkan apa yang ada di ruangan, lalu di mana letaknya. *There is a sofa in the living room. There is a TV on the wall. My cat is under the sofa.*

rows.en: There is a bed in my room.
There are two pictures on the wall.
There is a small table next to the bed.
rows.id: Ada meja kecil di sebelah tempat tidur.

rows.en: There are some shoes under the bed.
rows.id: Ada beberapa sepatu di bawah tempat tidur.

rows.en: My desk is between the window and the door.
rows.id: Mejaku di antara jendela dan pintu.

options: In the wall have a TV.
There is a TV on the wall.
There is a TV in on the wall.
blocks.explain: Use there is + the thing + one preposition: There is a TV on the wall. 'have' doesn't work here, and 'in on' has two prepositions.

id.explain: Pakai there is + bendanya + satu preposisi: There is a TV on the wall. 'have' tidak cocok di sini, dan 'in on' memakai dua preposisi.
